mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National identity-issuing authority of the country of origin (passport authority, interior ministry or civil registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961) plus sworn translation into Spanish by a translator authorized by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs or consular authorities; full consular legalization at the Spanish Consulate is required if the country of origin is not an Apostille signatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Incumbency (Certificado de vigencia o de titularidad) for any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or equivalent corporate register of the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-signatory countries, accompanied by a certified sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference or blocked-account deposit certificate evidencing the availability and lawful provenance of funds for the share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed credit institution of the shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial attestation or apostilled certified copy, with sworn Spanish translation where the original is not issued in Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of no criminal record (Certificado de antecedentes penales) or sworn declaration of absence of criminal history for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice, national police or equivalent competent authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization with sworn Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial power of attorney (Poder general o especial) appointing the incorporation representative in Spain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the jurisdiction of origin, duly legalized in accordance with the Hague Convention
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille followed by protocolización (binding of the document by a Spanish notary) for use in the escritura de constitución

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives and UBOs against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) EU Council CFSP sanctions lists with direct effect in Spain; (iii) OFAC SDN List as a best practice whenever any US nexus exists; (iv) SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales) warning indicators; and (v) national prohibitions under Ley 10/2010. Enhanced due diligence (EDD), including independent source-of-funds verification and senior-management approval, is mandatory for PEPs and for UBOs resident in high-risk third states pursuant to Article 14 Ley 10/2010. The obliged entity (Spanish counsel or incorporation agent) must document all screening results, retain records for at least ten (10) years, and apply risk-based continuous monitoring.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – online negative-name certificate application via www.rmc.es (Colegio de Registradores de España)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The denominación social must be written in Latin characters and pronounceable in Spanish; Spanish orthography governs vowels and consonants. A name derived from a non-Latin script must be transliterated into the Spanish/Latin alphabet. Words in other EU official languages are permitted only when rendered in Spanish script. The full corporate name must end with 'S.L.', 'Sociedad de Limitada' or 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada'. Homonymy with any existing name recorded in the Spanish or EU commercial registers is prohibited.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: España, Estado, Gobierno, Banco de España, Ministerio, Real, Nacional, Oficial – require prior written authorization of the corresponding ministry or public institution
Internacional (and linguistic equivalents) – requires evidence of prior or planned genuine international activity
Professional regulated designations (Auditor, Abogado, Notario, Corredor, Médico) – require prior colegial membership authorization
Financial or insurance activity tokens (Banco, Caja, Crédito, Aseguradora, Fondos, Inversión) – require prior Banco de España or Dirección General de Seguros licensing
Terms contrary to law, public order, or socially offensive words – absolutely prohibited
Denominations that are false, misleading, or suggestive of a different legal form than the SL
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Under Real Decreto 158/2008 the negative name certificate cannot be extended; after expiry of the 90-day reservation a new request must be filed. If the requested denomination is rejected, the applicant may (i) immediately file a modified request for an alternative denomination; (ii) within one (1) month of notification file a recurso de alzada administrative appeal before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice, attaching the original denial resolution and a prioritized list of alternative names; and (iii) if the appeal is dismissed, initiate judicial review before the Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Audiencia Nacional within two (2) months. Legal counsel should conduct a pre-screen against the RMC database at www.rmc.es before filing to avoid repeated rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual or mail-only office is not permissible as the statutory domicilio social of an SL. Article 9 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010) requires a genuine physical address in Spanish territory where administration is effectively carried out or where the business is established. Coworking centers and serviced offices are acceptable where a lease or license agreement evidences real occupancy and correspondence handling, but the address must be determinable and verifiable by the Registro Mercantil and AEAT.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced inspections: approximately 2%–5% within the first 12 months of incorporation. AEAT may verify the fiscal domicile, and SEPBLAC may conduct on-site AML compliance inspections only when risk alerts arise. For ISIC 6201 (software/cloud) with Low_Risk_Standard AML tier and no statutory license requirement, an unannounced visit is improbable absent red flags, but the registered office must be capable of receiving official notifications at all times.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley de Sociedades de Capital, Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, Articles 1-4 and 29-34
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escribano de Protocolo - Escritura de Constitución
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum paid-up capital of 3,000 euros, fully subscribed and deposited in a Spanish bank account prior to registration
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the Company, convened and acting unanimously, resolves: The sole shareholder has subscribed the entire share capital amounting to three thousand euros (EUR 3,000). The registered office is fixed at [full address]. The following officers are appointed: Managing Director [Name], Corporate Secretary [Name], and one Administrator [Name]. This resolution authorizes the filing of the incorporation documents with the Registro Mercantil, the payment of statutory fees, and the initiation of all necessary procedures for the company's legal existence and operation. All directors are empowered to perform any acts required for the incorporation and commencement of business activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Articles of Association and Share Subscription Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the articles of association specifying share classes, rights, obligations, and capital structure. Execute the share subscription agreement confirming full capital contribution. Have all documents reviewed and signed by the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend documents to address notary queries and resubmit for authentication

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request minor corrections and refile with the notary

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central or Provincial via online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the original notarized deed, articles, and supporting documents through the official portal or in person. Pay registration fees and obtain the certificate of registration and mercantile inscription.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any formal deficiencies and resubmit within the prescribed period

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide additional documentation or appeal to the competent tax authority if application is queried

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ERP and CRM software development

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharges, wastewater, or emissions generated; standard office waste disposal compliance applies only

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for non-industrial software operations; general occupational health and safety regulations apply

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); Sede Electrónica: https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; mandatory enrolment in the Census of Obligated Taxpayers ('Censo de Obligados Tributarios') via Modelo 036/037; digital mandates executed with Spanish electronic certificate (DNIe/FNMT) or EU eIDAS certificate.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Upon execution of the SL public deed, the notary applies for the provisional NIF (current format A/B + 8 digits + control). The definitive NIF is issued by the AEAT local tax office (Delegación de Grandes Contribuyentes if turnover exceeds EUR 6M) after registration in the Mercantile Registry, normally within 1 month. The SL must file Modelo 036 (declaration of commencement, modification, and registration in the census) within 1 month of deed execution, declaring both Corporate Income Tax (IS) and VAT (IVA) obligations. For a foreign entity without a permanent establishment making Spanish supplies: obtain a non-resident NIF (prefixed 'N') via Modelo 036/030 in person or through a mandatory fiscal representative (for non-EU residents), plus register for IVA under Art. 164 LIVA. For this ES_SL entity, the standard path is: certificate of incorporation + tax census form + electronic certificate application; no minimum capital filing fee applies (minimum capital: EUR 1); the SL may qualify for the 15% 'Highly Innovative Enterprise' rate under Ley 28/2022 subject to AEAT prior verification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — Spanish resident SL is a separate taxable person subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (IS) on worldwide income at 25% headline rate; newly incorporated SLs with active business income enjoy 15% rate for the first two tax periods before entering profitability; territorial scope is worldwide for tax-resident entities (with unilateral and treaty-based foreign tax credit); branch of a non-resident would instead be subject to IRNR on Spanish-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Spain. Available statutory elections: (i) Group taxation (régimen de consolidación fiscal) — optional where the parent holds at least 75% voting interest (70% if wholly owned subsidiaries are listed), irrevocable for 3 years, requires AEAT application; (ii) Reduced 15% startup rate under Ley 28/2022 — election made by filing Modelo 036 and satisfying quantitative criteria (entity age ≤5 years, or ≤7 years for biotech/emerging tech, R&D expenditure ratio, annual turnover ≤ EUR 10M, not resulting from a corporate restructuring); (iii) Patent box regime (Art. 23 LIS) with a 60% partial exemption on qualifying IP income at effective 10% CIT (must be elected within the corporate tax return, substantiated with contemporaneous documentation); (iv) ATAD 2 hybrid/mismatch rules are mandatory and do not require election; (v) Deductibility of economic rights and currency hedging — optional IFRS/tax accounting method elections filed in the annual tax return.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido) — Spanish value added tax fully harmonized with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis threshold: any natural or legal person carrying out taxable economic activity in Spanish territory must obtain a VAT number and file Modelo 036 before commencement (Art. 164 LIVA). Special SME exemption regime in force since 1 January 2025 (transposing EU Directive 2020/285): domestic micro-businesses with annual turnover ≤ EUR 85,000 are exempt (optional) and need not invoice VAT; intra-Community distance sales of goods and remotely supplied electronic services to EU consumers trigger Spanish VAT once annual EU-wide cross-border turnover exceeds EUR 10,000 (the OSS scheme is then optional). For the ISIC 6201 vertical SaaS activity, VAT registration is mandatory from the first B2B supply in Spain, irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2B electronic invoicing is mandatory under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and implementing RD 1007/2023, which entered 18 December 2023: all invoices issued to Spanish entrepreneurs must be in a structured electronic format (XML) compliant with the 'Facturae' standard or the AEAT-defined interoperability schema. Large enterprises (turnover > EUR 8M) must issue/transmit/receive e-invoices within 12 months of the regulation's effective trigger; all other businesses (including the present SL) have a 24-month transition from the same trigger (expected full phase-in by 2027). The AEAT provides a free public platform (Servicio de Facturación Electrónica, SFE) and API endpoints (SOAP/REST with certificates) for invoice exchange and registration; the SL must also maintain the VAT ledger records in electronic format under the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) regime if its annual turnover exceeds EUR 6M, submitting transaction-level records to AEAT within 4 business days (8 for issued invoices) of each invoicing event. For B2C transactions, no national real-time clearance mandate is yet in force, but Basque Country/Foral territories are piloting TicketBAI; the SL should implement e-invoice APIs compliant with RD 1007/2023 from day one.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For the SL's vertical ERP/CRM B2B cloud services: zero-rate (exemption with right of deduction) under Art. 70.Uno.1º LIVA when the recipient is an entrepreneur or professional established in a third country or in another EU Member State and the service is not deemed to be used/exploited in Spanish territory; the supplier must obtain the customer's EU VAT ID (validated via VIES) or, for non-EU customers, a tax residence certificate or equivalent official document evidencing establishment outside Spain, plus a signed statement/contract clauses confirming the business purpose and place of effective use; for B2C electronic services (cloud software to final consumers), Spanish VAT applies unless the customer is established in a non-EU country (then zero-rated); intra-EU B2C supplies are taxed in the Member State of the consumer under the Union OSS scheme. Tangible goods exports (if any hardware bundled with the subscription) qualify under Art. 21 LIVA only where goods physically leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch and are covered by an accepted export declaration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DUA — Documento Único Administrativo) with AEAT customs office discharge stamp/electronic acceptance record
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR, or equivalent transport document evidencing physical departure of goods outside EU customs territory (required only for goods exports, not pure SaaS)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa / SWIFT MT103) from the Spanish paying bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a Spanish account within the repatriation window
Validated customer VAT identification number (VIES printout for EU counterparties; Certificate of Tax Residence for non-EU counterparties) together with the signed contract or purchase order
Service delivery records proving the place of use/exploitation (IP logs, subscriber location data, performance milestones) for services and SaaS subscriptions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may reopen a zero-rated supply within the general 4-year limitation period (Art. 66 LGT; extended to 10 years where the concealment is fraudulent or involves a going-concern aimed at tax evasion). Where zero-rating is rejected, the SL is assessed for 21% IVA on the invoice amount plus legal late-payment interest (interés de demora, approx. 4.07% in 2025) and penalty per Arts. 191–193 LGT: 50% of the tax amount for non-deliberate errors; 100% where concealment exists; up to 150% in cases of fraud. Input VAT improperly deducted or refunded is clawed back with interest, and the directors may be declared jointly liable under Art. 42.2 LGT. Criminal liability (Art. 305 Código Penal) applies where the defrauded IVA quota exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period: imprisonment of 1 to 5 years, fines of up to six times the defrauded amount, loss of subsidies and public procurement rights for up to 5 years. The SL must preserve the export documentation bundle for at least 6 years (complete retention cycle covering the statute of limitations plus possible appeals) and submit the annual recapitulative statement (Modelo 349) for intra-EU services if applicable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the Eurosystem and the European Union framework; foreign-exchange and external-reporting rules also involve the Spanish Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise and applicable EU sanctions authorities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain uses the euro, which is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions within the applicable EU legal framework. A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may generally receive foreign investment, hold foreign-currency accounts, acquire foreign assets, make cross-border payments, distribute dividends, repay shareholder loans, and remit profits without prior exchange-control approval. Payments remain subject to ordinary corporate-law, tax, anti-money-laundering, sanctions, transfer-pricing, withholding-tax, beneficial-ownership, and financial-reporting requirements. Dividend distributions require distributable profits, appropriate financial statements and corporate approvals; Spanish withholding tax and treaty or EU exemptions must be assessed before remittance. Banks may require evidence of the legal purpose, source of funds, tax treatment, ownership chain, and underlying commercial documentation. Certain foreign investments, regulated-sector investments, sanctions-related transactions, and transactions involving restricted jurisdictions may require notification, authorization, or enhanced diligence. Spanish residents and companies may also have statistical or informational reporting obligations for external assets, liabilities, and transactions, depending on thresholds and reporting programs applicable at the relevant time.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain has no general statutory requirement for exporters to surrender export proceeds to Banco de España and no general mandatory conversion ratio or fixed conversion deadline for export receipts. Export proceeds may generally remain in euros or foreign currency and may be retained in domestic or foreign accounts, subject to banking, accounting, tax, sanctions, and statistical-reporting obligations. The company should maintain contracts, invoices, shipping or service-delivery evidence, customer payment records, and reconciliation records. Banks may request transaction-level explanations under anti-money-laundering and payment-screening procedures. Currency conversion should be performed when commercially required, with appropriate accounting recognition and documentation of realized or unrealized foreign-exchange gains and losses.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium to High for payment collection, SEPA transfers, card acquiring, and treasury operations where the provider is an EU or EEA-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution with valid Spanish passporting and safeguarding arrangements. An offshore or third-country digital EMI has no automatic right to provide regulated payment services in Spain; it generally requires an EU-authorized entity, a Spanish branch or agent where applicable, or another lawful licensing and passporting structure. EMI-held funds are safeguarded customer funds and are not equivalent to deposits covered by the Spanish deposit-guarantee scheme. Fintech accounts may be unsuitable as the sole account for statutory capital evidence, complex shareholder funding, large intercompany flows, cash management, foreign-exchange dealing, or transactions requiring correspondent-bank support. The company should confirm provider authorization in the relevant EBA or Bank of Spain register, safeguarding model, country coverage, settlement limits, sanctions policy, account-closure rights, and data-access procedures.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a branch to open a corporate account. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified electronic identification, video identification, electronic signatures, notarized or apostilled documents, and bank-approved verification procedures. Each bank determines its own risk policy. The bank may require a live video interview, certified copies, a Spanish notarial power of attorney, an in-person appearance by an authorized signatory or beneficial owner, or branch attendance where the ownership chain, source of funds, jurisdictional exposure, activity profile, or document quality creates enhanced-risk indicators. Directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, and controlling persons should be prepared to complete individual KYC even when the account is opened remotely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent corporate records, including mismatch between the Mercantile Registry, articles of association, tax identification records, shareholder register, bank mandate, or beneficial-owner declaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recent certified Mercantile Registry extract; deed of incorporation and articles of association; current shareholder and beneficial-owner chart; director and signatory resolutions; Spanish tax identification evidence; registry certificates for foreign shareholders; notarized, apostilled, and translated documents where required; written explanation of any name, address, ownership, or management discrepancy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee arrangements, layered holding companies, trusts, foundations, or beneficial owners located in multiple jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership tree to the natural-person beneficial owners; constitutional documents for every relevant entity; registers of shareholders and directors; trust or foundation instruments where applicable; passports and proof of address for beneficial owners and controllers; ownership attestations; independent corporate database extracts; legal memorandum explaining control and voting rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder capital injection or shareholder loan with unclear source of funds, unexplained intermediary banks, or a transfer amount inconsistent with the business plan.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed capital-increase or shareholder-loan agreement; corporate approval; bank statements showing origin of funds; audited or management financial statements of the funding entity; tax returns or income evidence where appropriate; payment message; funding-flow chart; source-of-wealth statement for relevant individuals; business plan and capitalization schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Software business model involving high transaction volumes, recurring payments, customer funds, marketplace activity, virtual assets, gaming, adult content, sanctioned territories, or activities that could constitute regulated payment services.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product and funds-flow memorandum; customer and supplier geography; terms of service; invoicing and subscription model; confirmation that the company does not hold customer funds or provide regulated payment services; licenses or legal opinions where relevant; payment-processor agreements; transaction-monitoring procedures; sanctions and prohibited-business policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border flows to or from Latin America, Asia, the Middle East, or other jurisdictions classified by the bank as enhanced-risk, including unusual currency, payment routing, or third-party settlement patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-by-country transaction forecast; customer and supplier list; contracts, invoices, purchase orders, and delivery evidence; expected monthly volumes and currencies; explanation of correspondent banks and payment intermediaries; sanctions-screening procedure; enhanced due-diligence files for material counterparties; reconciliation and exception-escalation policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of personal accounts, unrelated third-party accounts, cash payments, payment aggregators, or frequent transfers lacking a clear contractual relationship.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written prohibition on personal and unrelated third-party settlement; approved payment matrix; counterparty master data; contract and invoice matching; bank reconciliation procedures; explanation and remediation plan for historical exceptions; board-approved treasury policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-office, operating address, directors, or beneficial owners located outside Spain without credible evidence of Spanish substance or operational activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or office-service agreement; employee or contractor records; Spanish tax registrations; customer and supplier contracts; website and product documentation; management activity evidence; accounting records; local professional-adviser confirmations; explanation of the Spanish entity's functions and decision-making process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, politically exposed person status, sanctions exposure, criminal allegations, tax disputes, or inconsistent public information concerning a director, owner, or major counterparty.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Identity and role clarification; independent reputable-source review; court or regulatory clearance documents where available; explanation of the matter and current status; sanctions-screening evidence; PEP risk assessment; enhanced approval by the bank's compliance function; documented mitigation and ongoing monitoring plan.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Open the Spanish corporate account before funding where practicable and use a regulated bank or EU-authorized payment institution. Route the transfer from the shareholder's or investor's own account, preferably through a bank in the same legal name as the documented funder. Identify the payment as share capital, share-premium contribution, or shareholder loan, and use a clear free-text purpose such as 'capital contribution to Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or 'shareholder loan under agreement dated [date]'. Where a bank or payment system requires a purpose code, select the code corresponding to equity investment, capital contribution, or shareholder financing; Spanish banks may apply internal codes rather than a single universally applicable public code. Obtain the SWIFT payment message, sender and beneficiary details, intermediary-bank information, and proof of source of funds. For a formal capital increase, coordinate the deposit or escrow certificate, notarial deed, shareholder resolutions, registry filing, accounting entry, and release of funds. For shareholder loans, maintain the executed agreement, arm's-length interest analysis, maturity and repayment terms, transfer-pricing support, and withholding-tax assessment. Reconcile the receipt to the shareholder ledger and retain documents for AML, tax, accounting, and statistical-reporting purposes. SEPA Credit Transfer may be used for euro payments from participating institutions; SWIFT cross-border wires remain appropriate for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA scheme, subject to bank limits and beneficiary verification. Use SWIFT cross-border payment instructions for non-SEPA currencies or jurisdictions; the bank may process the payment through correspondent banks and use the applicable ISO 20022 message or legacy MT103 during any permitted transition. Match each payment to an approved vendor, contract, purchase order, invoice, tax documentation, and delivery or service evidence. For material or higher-risk purchases, use a commercial documentary letter of credit issued or advised by a regulated bank, with defined Incoterms, documentary conditions, presentation period, discrepancy rules, sanctions screening, and confirmation requirements. Documentary collections, bank guarantees, and open-account payments may be used according to counterparty risk. Use SEPA Direct Debit for recurring customer collections only with valid creditor identification, compliant mandate records, pre-notification, and applicable Core or Business-to-Business scheme controls. Stripe or another regulated payment service provider may support billing and collection but should not be treated as a substitute for a bank account or a licensed treasury function. Screen beneficiaries, counterparties, vessels, countries, goods, and payment narratives against applicable EU, Spanish, United Nations, United Kingdom, and United States sanctions where contractually or operationally relevant.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with an authorized credit institution or appropriately authorized investment firm, supported by an identified commercial exposure, documented treasury policy, counterparty limit, confirmation, valuation, and settlement process.

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where delivery is restricted or impractical, subject to counterparty authorization, local-law restrictions, applicable EU financial-markets rules, collateral terms, reporting, and evidence of a genuine underlying exposure.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval, ISDA or equivalent documentation, collateral arrangements, valuation controls, EMIR classification and reporting requirements, and appropriate accounting treatment.
Foreign-exchange spot transactions for ordinary operational conversion, subject to bank onboarding, sanctions screening, transaction monitoring, and accurate accounting.

Currency options, collars, and other structured hedges only after suitability, complexity, cost, fair-value, collateral, termination, and downside-risk review; retail-style or speculative trading should be prohibited under the corporate treasury policy.

The company should not offer FX products to customers or execute transactions for third parties unless separately authorized under applicable Spanish and EU financial-services laws. Hedging documentation should identify the exposure, hedge objective, notional, tenor, currency pair, approved counterparty, valuation source, accounting designation, and responsible approver.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Provincial Mercantile Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of approval at the shareholders' general meeting; approval must occur within six months of fiscal year-end (for 31 Dec year-end: approval by 30 June, filing by 31 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, suspension of registry filings, and after repeated non-compliance, administrative strike-off and closure of corporate tax records

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months and 25 days after the fiscal year-end (for 31 Dec year-end: 25 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges of 5%, 10% or 15% of tax due depending on delay, plus statutory interest; base fixed penalty from EUR 120 up to the tax amount

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Information Return on Third-Party Transactions (Modelo 347) – required if payments/collections with any counterparty exceed EUR 3,005.06 during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 28 February of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of EUR 100 per data item, with a minimum of EUR 1,500, and up to EUR 15,000 or 2% of turnover for substantial inaccuracies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Declaración de Titularidad Real) submitted with annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil via the Annual Accounts deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as Annual Accounts deposit (31 July for a calendar year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to disclose accurate beneficial ownership may block registry filings, trigger fines up to EUR 100,000, and preclude director clearance procedures

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for SL if at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets > EUR 2,850,000; net annual turnover > EUR 5,700,000; average headcount > 50 employees. Lower thresholds apply for groups.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) aligned with EU-adopted IFRS for consolidated groups; Local GAAP for individual financial statements

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All shareholding transfers, changes in control, and any other modifications to beneficial ownership must be recorded in the internal Beneficial Ownership Register (Libro de Titularidades Reales) and reported to the Mercantile Registry when filing the annual accounts. The annual accounts filing includes a mandatory beneficial ownership confirmation section; at least one individual must be specifically identified as the final beneficial owner, and any modifications during the year must be contemporaneously entered and subsequently certified.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Beneficial Ownership Register (Libro de Titularidades Reales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 1,000–EUR 2,500 (approx. USD 1,100–2,750) for commercial registered office and annual corporate secretarial services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 2,800–EUR 6,500 (approx. USD 3,000–7,000) for a statutory audit of a Spanish SL when audit thresholds are met, dependent on company size and file complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% corporate income tax rate for newly created entities on the first €300,000 of taxable income for the first two profitable tax years; R&D and innovation tax credits up to 25%; 100% amortisation for certain information-technology-related intangible assets; exemption for qualified participation in Spanish and non-Spanish subsidiaries subject to holding period and substance requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Declaración del Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically via the AEAT Sede Electrónica; applicable to Spanish-resident entities and permanent establishments of non-residents.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the tax year-end (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, filing window is 1 July to 25 July).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer NIF and full legal name.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the NIF-ES assigned to the Spanish permanent establishment; non-residents without a permanent establishment should not file Form 200.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the permanent establishment's Spanish tax-period dates; generally mirror the taxpayer's fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the accounting result attributable to the permanent establishment's Spanish activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after conversion from accounting result, including prior-year loss offsets and required adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute using separate PE accounts; include transfer-pricing adjustments relevant to Spanish activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate / full tax liability section
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Liability at 25% corporate income tax rate before credits and payments on account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same rate to income effectively connected with the permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings, instalments, and payments made during the tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include Spanish-source withholdings suffered by the permanent establishment and any quarterly prepayments made under Form 202.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable to the Treasury or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Remit the balance by direct debit or bank transfer from the PE's Spanish account; non-residents without a PE must use Form 210/213/216 as applicable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior AEAT demand: graduated surcharge of 5% (up to 3 months), 10% (3-6 months), 15% (6-12 months) or 20% (over 12 months) of the tax due, plus late interest; incorrect or omitted data carries €150 per item; more serious concealment can trigger an administrative penalty of 50%-150% of the tax base and criminal prosecution for tax evasion where the evaded amount exceeds €120,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must obtain a Spanish tax residence certificate from the home-state tax authority, provide it to the Spanish SL before payment (or invoke the relevant double-taxation agreement), and use Form 210 to claim refund where the SL has withheld at the domestic rate. The paying SL must generally withhold and report through Form 216. Under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, 0% withholding may apply if the shareholder holds at least 5% of the SL for at least 12 months; proof of holding and substance must be submitted to the AEAT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rate: 19% for both interest and IP royalties paid to non-residents; treaty rates generally cap interest at 10% and royalties at 10%; under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, 0% withholding applies to related EU companies holding directly at least 25% for two consecutive years.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: required for related-party transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 per category in the tax period; Master File: required where consolidated group turnover exceeds EUR 45,000,000 in the preceding year. Documentation must be prepared in Spanish or English and submitted/inspection-ready within 30 days of AEAT request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) analogous to the UAE regime, but Spanish law applies general anti-abuse rules, substance-over-form principles, CFC rules, and anti-treaty-shopping provisions under Article 15 LGT; the S.L. must maintain real personnel, premises, and business activity in Spain to sustain corporate residence, tax credits, and participation exemptions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion (Infracción / Delito contra la Hacienda Pública)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to declare Spanish-source cloud software revenue, artificial routing of licence income through tax-haven affiliates, or creation of false invoices to reduce taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50%-150% of the tax base plus late interest; criminal liability where the evaded amount exceeds €120,000, punishable by 1-5 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to six times the evaded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who consent to or order the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt, may lose management rights, and may be subject to travel bans and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unadjusted internal prices for cloud services, SaaS licences, or management fees with offshore related parties, or failing to prepare and retain Local File/Master File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income and penalty of 20% of the resulting tax assessment; separate penalties of up to 15% of the transaction amount for missing or defective documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in approving non-arm's-length terms can be held personally liable in insolvency or for the deficit caused, with possible disqualification and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of Legal Form
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the S.L. with no employees, no office, no Spanish management, no operational substance, or using it solely to strip profits as dividends or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization under general anti-abuse rules, denial of tax treaty benefits, loss of retained tax credits, penalty of up to 150% of the underpaid tax, and potential judicial order to close the company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly liable for corporate tax debts arising from evasion; courts may impose management disqualification, seizing of personal assets, and travel bans pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating cloud payment rails (Stripe Billing, Direct Debit) without adequate customer due diligence, suspicious-transaction reporting, or internal AML controls, particularly where non-resident shareholders or clients are in high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Law 10/2010 of EUR 60,001 to EUR 5,000,000 for serious infringements; criminal money-laundering penalties up to six years' imprisonment and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally criminally liable for intentional AML violations; civil liability for damages, travel bans, and disqualification may be imposed.
